transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-08
Time: 08:00 PST / 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Meyers (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Evelyn Cortez (Auryn Head of ML), Marcus Li (Auryn Platform Eng), Priya Nair (Auryn Product)

Summary: Quick scoping for a 3-week POC: shortlist open models, define success criteria (latency/cost/accuracy), workload sizing, bench plan and timelines. Agreed to run small infra-backed bench on Redwood hosted + optional private VPC flow.

Topics: model shortlist, multilingual support (EN/ES + de/zh-lite), domain coverage (financial risk scoring + doc summarization), latency SLOs, batching/quantization tradeoffs, benchmark metrics and artifacts to collect.

(Notes: recording auto-transcribe; some words imperfect — e.g., "KV cache" appears as "K-V cash" in parts)

[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — can you hear me okay?
[00:05] Evelyn (Auryn): Yep, loud and clear. Morning.
[00:09] Jordan: Cool. Quick intros — Samir's our inference SE, he'll own bench configs.
[00:14] Samir (Redwood): Hi all. I'll lead the performance side, and we'll hand off scripts for you to run in your env if you want private bench.
[00:22] Marcus (Auryn): Great, Marcus here — I'll handle infra and networking, want to understand VPC options.
[00:28] Priya (Auryn): Priya — product, focused on latency and throughput for customer-facing features.
[00:34] Jordan: Perfect. Goal today: agree success criteria and pick 2-3 open models to exercise across Auryn's workloads — must include multilingual and long-context summarization cases.

[01:02] Samir: To set expectations, typical tradeoffs: bigger models => better quality but higher latency/cost; quantized 4-bit can cut cost ~2-3x but may hit subtle accuracy regressions on domain-specific financial language.
[01:22] Evelyn: Yeah; our core must keep financial entity extraction and risk-score consistency. If quantization breaks entity linking that's a no-go.
[01:31] Jordan: Understood. Proposed shortlist: LLaMA-3-13B (int8 and 4-bit variants), Mistral-Instruct-7B, and a multilingual variant — e.g., XLM-R-backed instruction-tuned or a LLaMA-3 multilingual fork. Also optionally try an emergent 30B from community for long-form summarization.
[01:56] Priya: Can you say the names again? We have used some internal names before, sometimes transcription swaps them.
[02:04] Jordan: Sure — LLaMA-3 13B, Mistral Instruct 7B, and a multilingual 13B variant (we'll include a 30B as stretch for long context).

[02:30] Marcus: For throughput: average concurrent users 120, typical request length 80 tokens, sometimes up to 1200 tokens for summaries. Peak qps ~40. We need P95 latency under 800ms for short prompts, and for long summaries we'd accept up to 6s on hosted.
[02:56] Samir: Good to know. We'll size bench runs for 1) peaky short requests, 2) long summarization with KV cache warm start, and 3) batch inference for nightly backfill. We'll capture tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 latency, GPU util, and cost-per-1k-tokens.

[03:30] Evelyn: Security: Auryn needs SOC2-like artefacts, audit logs, KMS integration for keys. Private deployment is possible but prefer Redwood dedicated if infra fits. Can you confirm Redwood has KMS/HSM options?
[03:48] Jordan: Yes, Redwood Private supports customer KMS via AWS KMS and bring-your-own keys; we also have audit log exports and SSO (SAML) options. I'll share the security pack link after the call.
[03:59] Evelyn: Perfect. That'll be key for our procurement.

[04:12] Samir: Regarding bench infra choices — two paths: 1) Redwood hosted (fastest to run) where we spin up test models in a sandbox; 2) Private runner in your VPC (Marcus configures subnets, we provide container image and probe). Private runs add latency for setup but match your network egress and KMS flows.
[04:36] Marcus: We prefer private for final acceptance tests, hosted is fine for initial profiling.

[05:02] Jordan: On metrics: primary success criteria set by Auryn?
[05:07] Priya: Primary: quality (F1 over labelled entity extraction > 0.87 for finance entities), secondary: latency (P95 < 800ms for short queries), tertiary: cost (target <$0.008 per 1k tokens for production). These are ballpark — we can refine with actual bench numbers.
[05:27] Samir: We'll run targeted evals against your gold labels to compute F1, exact match for key fields, and also run end-to-end regression tests on a sample of 200 docs.

[05:58] Jordan: For multilingual: languages are en, es primary; de and zh-lite as lower priority. Do you have labelled data in those?
[06:08] Evelyn: We have labelled Spanish and a small German set, Chinese is sparse. So we need model performance that degrades gracefully — if multilingual variant fails we might fallback to language-specific smaller models for ES.
[06:26] Samir: We'll include translation+instruct baseline: translate-to-en then run english model as a fallback to set expectations. That will show latency/cost tradeoffs for multilingual.

[06:47] Marcus: Bench timeline?
[06:50] Jordan: Plan: Week 0 (this week): agree on shortlist and artifacts. Week 1: Redwood sets up hosted benches and sends scripts; Auryn shares prompt sets. Week 2: Run private VPC bench and end-to-end accuracy checks. Week 3: Consolidate metrics, run canary on a small production slice. So roughly 3 weeks.
[07:17] Evelyn: That aligns with our internal timeline; must have procurement sign-off before canary.

[07:30] Priya: For the long-context summaries — how will you measure coherence vs hallucination?
[07:35] Samir: We'll use two measures: 1) ROUGE-like overlap with gold summary and 2) a small annotation pass (20 docs) checking hallucination rate by human raters. Also measure chunking behavior: do we maintain entity consistency across long docs with KV cache enabled. Note: KV cache is sometimes transcribed as K-V cash in our auto notes.
[08:07] Jordan: On quantization and accuracy: we'll test int8, 4-bit and fp16 where possible. Expect stepwise latency gains but watch for subtle drop on entity linking with 4-bit on some models. We'll flag any >3% drop in F1 as unacceptable.

[08:32] Marcus: Can we get rough cost delta estimates per model?
[08:35] Jordan: High level: Mistral-7B quantized => lowest cost; LLaMA-3-13B int8 => mid; LLaMA-3-30B => high. We'll include per-1k-token cost with batch size ranges in the sheet.

[08:54] Evelyn: Any concerns on tokenization with finance jargon? Sometimes models split tickers oddly.
[08:59] Samir: We'll include tokenization diagnostics (token counts per prompt) as part of the bench outputs.

[09:12] Priya: Who will own the benchmark runner when we do private runs?
[09:15] Marcus: Marcus (Auryn) will run the container in our VPC, Samir will hand over scripts.
[09:20] Samir: Yes, we'll provide a docker image + k8s manifest and simple runner that outputs CSVs to a mounted EFS or S3 endpoint.

[09:34] Jordan: A few operational notes: Redwood supports autoscale burst to handle peak 60s of spiky load; we should test scaling under synthetic spike. Also include failure-mode tests: model fallback to smaller variant if GPU pool saturated.
[09:52] Evelyn: Fallback behaviour is important. We need deterministic routing — no surprising model switches without traffic-shaping rules.
[09:58] Jordan: Agreed, we'll show our routing policy config in the bench package.

[10:12] Priya: Regarding procurement — we'll need SOC2 type II, encryption in transit and at rest, SSO and audit logs. Marcus will follow procurement checklist.
[10:23] Jordan: I'll attach Redwood security pack and SOC2 report to the CRM record and send directly after this call.

[10:31] Evelyn: For the model shortlist, can you include one smaller high-quality instruct-tuned 3B so we can test a low-cost fall back?
[10:36] Samir: Yes — we'll add a 3B instruct (Mistral 3B or similar) as a baseline.

[10:44] Jordan: So final shortlist: Mistral-Instruct-3B baseline, Mistral-Instruct-7B, LLaMA-3-13B (int8 + 4-bit), LLaMA-3 multilingual 13B, stretch LLaMA-3-30B for long-context. We'll enumerate exact model IDs in the benchmark template.

[11:06] Marcus: For telemetry, we want per-token cost, GPU utilization, memory pressure, and p50/p95/p99 latencies across request shapes.
[11:15] Samir: We'll capture all of those plus tokenization profiles, and sample outputs for quality scoring. Exports will be in CSV + a consolidated PDF report.

[11:29] Jordan: Shared artifacts: Benchmark template (link: https://redwood.example.com/benchmarks/template-auryn), Security pack (link: https://redwood.example.com/security/pack), Pricing deck (link: https://redwood.example.com/pricing/auryn). We'll also create a shared gdrive sheet: "Auryn POC Bench - Tracker" and put the sample prompts there.

[11:58] Evelyn: Great. One more question: for the nightly batch backfill, do you recommend dedicated GPUs or can hosted pooled capacity handle it?
[12:06] Samir: Nightly backfills are cheaper on dedicated reserved capacity; hosted is fine for short runs but if you have sustained nightly windows, Dedicated commit might lower unit costs. We'll quantify in the cost estimate.

[12:23] Priya: Ok — recap and next steps?
[12:27] Jordan: Recap: agree shortlist, Redwood sends benchmark template + security pack + pricing by 2026-01-11; Auryn sends sample prompts and gold labels by 2026-01-12; schedule bench kickoff 2026-01-13 with Marcus. Action items assigned.

[12:46] Marcus: Sounds good. We'll also prepare a small VPC test subnet if needed.
[12:50] Evelyn: Thanks — talk soon.
[12:53] Jordan: Thanks everyone. Closing.

Post-call quick notes: transcription mislabels KMS as "K-M-S" in one spot and KV cache as "K-V cash". We will clean in CRM attachments.
